Study hour (150h)
= 45h contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
info.description:
This course, "Research for Designers," dives into the world of strategic design research. Students will explore qualitative and quantitative research techniques, the importance of data-driven design, and ethical considerations within the research process. This course teaches how to integrate these insights into design thinking, producing evidence-based solutions that resonate with the target audience.
By the end of the course, students will gain essential skills in critical analysis, research methodology, empathy building, evidence-based decision-making, and clear communication of findings. This course will transform students into more strategic, insightful, and user-focused designers, ready to tackle the complexities of real-world design challenges.
The course can also help students apply the knowledge they have gained in delivering scientific reports and build and develop report presentation skills at seminars and conferences.

- Read the textbook in advance
- Access the course website (https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/) for up-to-date information and material of the course.

clos.loDetails: Explain the importance of conducting human-centric research before making design decision, as well as basic definition of design research and design thinking
Apply essentials of design research to conduct a research proposal
Analyse different research methods and the level of appropriation of each method

Deliver the research report in a logical and easy-to-understand manner to other stakeholders
Demonstrate professionalism in conducting research and show respect for intellectual properties

- Student analyze and present the understanding and application of a part of theory
assessments.gradingGuide:
From session 3 to 18 - Group Presentation Requirements
Group size: Each group consists of 4–6 students.
Preparation: Work at home based on the course textbook and topics assigned by the instructor.
Presentation: In-class presentation of 25–30 minutes, followed by 5–10 minutes Q&A.
AI usage: AI tools are allowed (for research, analysis, slide design, images, charts, etc.), but the final work must demonstrate critical thinking, creativity, and originality.
Topics:
Design as Practice, Research, and Thinking
Research Essentials
Ethnographic Research
Qualitative Research
Quantitative Research
Visual Research
Presenting Your Research
